entries.reason: Candidate8 closed six independent audit findings covering post-commit finalize recovery, lock transition failures, offline migration atomicity, retry authority convergence, sink-capability bypasses, and immutable verification evidence.
entries.trigger: Exhaustive final audit of candidate7 failure boundaries and evidence integrity.
entries.resolution: Finalize teardown now journals exact flow identity and every durable phase, never compensates a committed audit, and resumes destructive and completion publication idempotently. Process-owned locks report ordered primary/cleanup failures with owner, phase, visibility, durability uncertainty, and residue. The rename migration validates all authorities before mutation and uses a durable all-target transaction with exact-byte rollback/recovery. Retry recovery enforces a one-way flow -> issue-log -> public-artifact convergence lattice with one canonical payload per grant and rejects divergence before mutation. The source guard tracks flow-path taint separately from sink capabilities through aliases, computed members, Reflect.apply, and callback bridges, with only exact owner-module allowlisting. Final external verification logs bind command output to one clean commit SHA and tree at both boundaries.

findings.rootCause: Cleanup treated every failure as pre-commit and had no durable phase authority after Git history changed.
findings.invariant: Once commit-durable is journaled, audit compensation is forbidden and every remaining destructive/publication phase is monotonic and retryable.

findings.rootCause: Publish/release/stale-removal cleanup failures were swallowed or lost transition state.
findings.invariant: Every failed transition preserves the primary failure first and exposes phase, owner, visible publication, durability uncertainty, and temp/visible residue after all cleanup attempts.

findings.rootCause: The migration applied independent files incrementally without a durable all-target recovery authority.
findings.invariant: All real non-hardlinked authorities and planned bytes are captured before mutation; apply/rollback indexes are durable and recovery accepts only exact original or planned bytes.

findings.rootCause: Resume checked grant presence without proving unique canonical payload equality or publication order across three authorities.
findings.invariant: A grant progresses only absent -> flow -> flow+issue -> flow+issue+public; duplicates, divergent payloads, and out-of-order presence fail before mutation.

findings.rootCause: The static guard followed direct callee names but not first-class filesystem sink capabilities.
findings.invariant: A finding requires both flow-path taint and sink capability taint, including namespace, computed property, Reflect.apply, and callback propagation; allowlisting is exact-path only.

findings.rootCause: Earlier final logs did not record a source commit and tree, so outputs could not be independently joined to immutable bytes.
findings.invariant: Each final external log records commit, tree, clean status, exact command, and UTC start/end; ending commit/tree/status must equal the prelude.
findings.red: candidate7 final logs lack commit/tree preludes

entries.reason: The foreign pending recovery tests modified private transaction budgets without recomputing the transaction fingerprint, allowing RETRY_RECOVERY_AUTHORITY_INVALID to satisfy a broad foreign/authority regex before foreign-flow validation. Kept the private transaction bytes and fingerprint valid, changed only current flow runId/issue/spec identity, asserted exact RETRY_RECOVERY_FOREIGN_AUTHORITY on direct budget, view, review, status, next-action, and gate surfaces, and retained byte-for-byte no-mutation checks.

A durable rolling-back migration journal could be reinterpreted as applied when all targets still contained planned bytes, and directory snapshots tracked only inode identity so same-inode non-target content drift passed preflight. Recovery is now phase-monotonic: rolling-back always continues reverse rollback and only applying adopts planned progress. Snapshot journal v3 persists mode and SHA-256 byte revision for every relevant file and exempts only transaction targets from recovery-time content comparison.

Active-flow mutations were serialized only by their private registry lock, accepted path-bearing spec IDs, ignored duplicate mode conflicts, and treated local/Git probe failures as evidence that stale entries were valid. Every add/remove/cleanStale now acquires the repository flow-operation barrier before the registry lock with owner-token borrowing, spec and mode authority is strict, and all local/Git probes fail closed without registry mutation.

The flow-state sink guard's arrow callback bridge parsed only single-line expression bodies and did not propagate callback capability through local .call/.bind aliases, allowing multiline and async fs.promises bridges to bypass detection. The guard now extracts brace-balanced block arrows and propagates callback capability plus argument offsets through aliases, .call, and .bind while retaining the exact owner allowlist.

The two-process retry fixture used a directory poll and an arbitrary five-second child readiness deadline. It passed alone in 435 ms but timed out only in the 100-file serial union before both child-ready files appeared, so the failure did not establish a retry recovery product defect.
entries.trigger: Candidate9 100-file pre-record serial union: 980/982 passed and the pre-lock barrier timed out.
entries.resolution: Replaced time-based file polling with a dedicated fd 3 handshake. Each child synchronously writes its exact PID before entering the barrier; the parent validates both PID signals, observes child error and exit events, and releases only after both children are actually ready. Failure cleanup releases the barrier and settles both child results.
entries.guardrailCandidate: Concurrent process fixtures must synchronize on an explicit child-ready channel and child lifecycle events, not infer readiness from completion within a fixed wall-clock interval.

entries.reason: The final Git-result audit found that both cherry-pick abort paths ignored a failed abort and could continue to detached-worktree cleanup without a durable authority for the still-mutated Git state. Outcome schema and cleanup journal v2 now preserve the exact abort result, publish abort-failed before halting, expose primary-first ordered failures, and permit only cleanup-only replay from the journal.

Lifecycle diagnostics for the retry concurrency union failure showed one child exiting before the retry lock with ACTIVE_FLOW_REGISTRY_BUSY while its sibling performed an active-flow registry read. ActiveFlowRegistry.load unnecessarily acquired the exclusive writer lock even though registry publication is atomic, creating reader-reader contention before the command's intended operation boundary.
entries.trigger: Candidate9 fresh 100-file union and exact same-order 8-file prefix with PID, exit, stderr, lock, transaction, artifact, and flow authority diagnostics.
entries.resolution: Registry reads now open and strictly parse the atomic visible file without acquiring writer mutation locks. Every attempt requires the visible pre-read identity, opened descriptor identity, and visible post-read identity to match. An atomic identity race permits at most two total attempts; a second race returns explicit ACTIVE_FLOW_REGISTRY_BUSY without mutation. Malformed or unknown documents fail immediately with no retry or rewrite. Real non-hardlinked file, exact entry schema, mode, and spec authority remain fail-closed; concurrent readers during writer rename observe only complete old or new documents. Add/remove/cleanStale repository-operation and registry writer lock ordering is unchanged.

entries.reason: Candidate9 completed the final failure-boundary audit across finalize teardown, detached rescue, retry recovery, offline migration, active-flow registry transactions, and flow-state sink discovery. The audit also classified every union failure before correction and retained only valid RED evidence.
entries.trigger: Pre-commit self-audit, source-level Git/result and authority review, focused regression union, and exact same-order failure reproduction.
entries.resolution: Finalize teardown is journal-first, phase-monotonic, OID-CAS protected, and resumable without repeating committed Git mutations. Detached rescue probes and CAS-updates the base ref, verifies temporary-worktree removal, preserves pre-outcome crashes, and durably orders cherry-pick plus abort failures before cleanup-only retry. Retry recovery rejects foreign current authority with exact codes while retaining valid transaction bytes. Offline migration journals byte revisions and modes, treats rolling-back as one-way, and rejects same-inode non-target drift. Active-flow writers acquire repository operation before registry lock, validate exact spec/mode and local/Git authority, while strict atomic readers remain lock-free and use a maximum-two-attempt pre/open/post identity protocol.
